These API changes do not establish complete multiplatform ten-minute maximum-load acceptance; the measured iPad result and Android limits are recorded separately in [physical validation](../docs/validation/physical-validation.json) and [the performance summary](stats-performance.md). Host timing, bypass comparisons, memory accounting, actual Android/iOS builds and the remaining device/listening checks are separate evidence. The cited Studio and unified-transport benchmarks are historical observations. In the pre-variation layout, effects buffers at 192 kHz used approximately 13.1 MiB and four maximum-size triple-bank transports used 8,627,712 bytes (8.23 MiB), excluding renderer voices and queues. Version 1.1.0 grows those four transports to 9,537,152 bytes (9.10 MiB) on the measured 64-bit macOS layout, an increase of 909,440 bytes; see [variation storage measurements](native-variation-validation.md#storage-and-callback-work). These structure sizes are not a new whole-process or physical-device measurement. Total accounting must also include renderer voices/tails, command queues, effects, bridge/canonical options and recovery peaks. The 32 MiB additional-memory target remains a target, not a certified bound for version 1.1.0.

link_fixes.original_markdown: Choose a held voice when the ending follows a player action instead of a fixed duration: motor, charge beam, pad or the last chord of a ceremony. `noteOn` starts a positive app-owned ID; `noteOff` begins release from the current level, and compatible `updateNote` edits ramp over 10 ms. Distinct IDs remain independent events with fixed gain. Reserve enough capacity for their releases and unrelated effects, and release on cancellation as well as ordinary key up. See the [held motor recipe](examples.md#sustained-game-motor) for retry/cleanup handling.

link_fixes.original_markdown: The two additional voice LFOs move filter cutoff, square PWM or sine FM index using sine/triangle shapes. Avoid deep/high-rate modulation with strong resonance or high-frequency FM; safe parameter clamping does not guarantee a pleasant or alias-free sound. The [two-LFO example](examples.md#two-voice-lfos) shows a filtered PWM pad.
